messages:
Evelyn (People Ops): Hey all — quick announcement: were kicking off a 6-month pilot for PTO Advance specifically for employees on temporary cross-border assignments (workvisas, short-term secondments). This is to reduce financial friction for people who need to take leave while abroad. Form + FAQ below. :earth_americas:

Priya Desai: Nice! who exactly is eligible?

Evelyn (People Ops): Eligibility (short version): 1) assignment must be >= 60 days and <= 12 months, 2) manager sign-off, 3) People Ops approval, 4) employee must be on Redwood payroll for the assignment period. Full criteria in the FAQ link.

Marcos Alvarez: If someone is on a remote workcation (still local payroll) are they included?

Evelyn (People Ops): Not by default. Remote workcations that do not change country/payroll are handled by standard PTO rules. This pilot is for cross-border pay/assignment situations where payroll/taxation could create cashflow issues.

Jamal Khan: Good. What about tax/reporting implications?

Finance Bot: Automated notice: Any PTO advance processed under this pilot will be recorded as an advance on payroll and may have tax/reporting implications depending on country of payroll. Finance will notify impacted employees with a country-specific note after approval.

Priya Desai: Is there a repayment schedule? e.g., if they leave before they use the advance?

Evelyn (People Ops): Repayment: the advance is reconciled against future accruals; if someone leaves before reconciliation, any outstanding advance is deducted from final pay per local law. Well surface this on the approval form and require acknowledgment.

Jamal Khan: Can we request retroactive advances for assignments that started last month?

Evelyn (People Ops): Yes — retro requests accepted up to 30 days after assignment start. For retro cases we need manager + People Ops sign-off and a short justification.

Priya Desai: Wheres the form?

Evelyn (People Ops): Form + FAQ: https://redwood.internal/hr/pto-advance-pilot (internal link) 
Form fields: name, employee ID, assignment country, assignment start/end, requested advance days, manager, reason.

Evelyn (People Ops): Quick process snippet:
```
1) Employee fills form
2) Manager approves in 48h
3) People Ops reviews (tax check) within 5 business days
4) Finance posts advance on payroll
```

Marcos Alvarez: If someone already used unpaid leave to cover travel costs, can they convert that to an advance?

Evelyn (People Ops): Well evaluate case-by-case. If approved, Finance will backdate as described and mark as conversion. Include the original dates and receipts in the form.

Priya Desai: Will this affect headcount/bench policies or resource planning?

Evelyn (People Ops): No change to headcount. Managers should still coordinate coverage as usual. This is purely a cashflow/compassion measure.

Finance Bot: FYI: For UK and EU assignments theres extra payroll complexity — Finance will reach out individually after People Ops approval.

Evelyn (People Ops): Were hosting a 30-min AMA Friday at 9am PST in #all-hands for any edge cases. If youd like us to review a specific scenario beforehand ping me or attach a note in the form. Thanks! :sparkles: 

Priya Desai: Thanks Evelyn — will share the link with my team.

Marcos Alvarez: Appreciated.

Jamal Khan: Thanks — good to see this option.

Evelyn (People Ops): Closing note: pilot runs for 6 months; well gather usage, finance impact, and satisfaction before deciding next steps. If you have feedback during the pilot, please DM me.
